clue.text: Outmatch former top tennis player, say

parts.note: ex- is a prefix meaning former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: say tells us the next piece is spoken, so we write letters that sound like it

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked tennis player in a tournament draw

explanation.surface: A one-time leading tennis star is beaten by someone better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks a sound-alike: the tennis word is heard, but written with a C, as in the verb meaning to go beyond.
explanation.definitionFit: To outmatch someone is to surpass or go beyond them, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Slightly well off? That's absurd

definitions.meaning: read literally: somewhat wealthy, a little rich
the idiom said of an unreasonable claim, especially a hypocritical one

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom read literally means a little wealthy, and as a phrase it is an exclamation of indignant disbelief.

clue.text: New wars or old weapons

indicators.note: new signals that the letters are formed afresh into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A choice between fresh conflicts and ancient arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot from bows, these were the missiles of medieval and earlier warfare.

clue.text: Fail to draw positive conclusions from Dante's work

parts.note: to infer is to draw conclusions from evidence
failing to be positive is a negative, a no

explanation.surface: Someone cannot find anything good to say about the Italian poet's writing.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase as a whole reads 'infer no', drawing a negative rather than positive conclusion.
explanation.definitionFit: The first part of Dante's Divine Comedy, the poet's journey through Hell, bears this title.

clue.text: Possibly fly in group

parts.note: taken as written
a sect is a group, often a religious faction

explanation.surface: A fly might join a set of followers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' marks fly as one example among many.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly is one example of a six-legged creature, hence the 'possibly'.

clue.text: Where everybody goes in to sweep around the floor

definitions.text: Where everybody goes in to sweep around the floor

indicators.note: goes in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: to broom is to sweep with a broom
all means everybody

explanation.surface: The dance venue where all the guests glide across the polished floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes in' signals the container. 'Sweep' looks like a verb of cleaning, but read as a whole the clue pictures dancers gliding round the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hall for dancing, where couples whirl across the floor together.

clue.text: In high spirits, using once socially accepted form of banter

parts.note: ex- means once, formerly
U is the old label for upper-class, socially acceptable usage

indicators.note: form of signals that the following word's letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone lively uses a jokey style of teasing that used to be polite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges BANTER into BERANT. U versus non-U was a 1950s British distinction of upper-class speech.
explanation.definitionFit: An exuberant person is full of energy and cheerfulness, which is high spirits.

clue.text: Where to keep one's hose readily available

definitions.meaning: a hose kept connected to a tap is ready for watering
on hand whenever needed, like beer drawn from a cask

explanation.definitionFit: A hose fitted to a tap is ready for use, and the phrase idiomatically means available immediately.

clue.text: Terry does badly in this craft

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man named Terry performs poorly in some skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' rearranges TERRYDOES. 'Craft' looks like a skill, but it means a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A destroyer is a fast naval warship, a kind of vessel or craft.

clue.text: An author's sources

definitions.meaning: H G ..., writer of The Time Machine; the 's stands for is
springs or bores from which water is drawn

explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the novelist H G Wells, and also places where water rises or is drawn up.

clue.text: He's a monster — and so regressive!

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, and so

explanation.surface: A beast who is also reactionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute from fairy tales who eats people is the monster in question.

clue.text: Extraordinary deed is opposed to current trends

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase for nouns: whirls of water running against the main stream

indicators.note: extraordinary suggests the letters are made into something unusual, a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An exceptional act goes against the fashions of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extraordinary' rearranges DEEDIS. 'Current trends' looks like fashion but is the flow of a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: These are swirls of water that circle back against the main flow of a stream.

clue.text: Denial in the form of no eating

indicators.note: in the form of signals the letters take a new shape

explanation.surface: Refusing food as a way of saying no.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying no to something or contradicting it is a denial.

clue.text: In which a performer has to take a bow

definitions.text: In which a performer has to take a bow

parts.words: In which a performer has to take a bow
parts.note: not a stage bow at the curtain but a longbow taken up to shoot at a target

explanation.definitionFit: The sport of shooting with a bow and arrows requires the competitor to pick one up.

clue.text: Ruling concerning double gin cocktails

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: cocktails are mixtures, so the letters are mixed
double means the word is taken twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A judgment about drinks made with twice the usual spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'double' gives GINGIN, which 'cocktails' rearranges into IGNING.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch on the throne is ruling, as is a current champion.

clue.text: Defeat in game at home

parts.note: RU is rugby union
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A loss suffered in a home fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin an opponent is to wreck or defeat them; the noun works as well.

clue.text: When to tuck in?

parts.note: not eating heartily but tucking a child into bed

explanation.definitionFit: The hour when children are put to bed and the covers tucked around them.

clue.text: Learnt to become easy-going

indicators.note: become signals the letters turning into something else

explanation.surface: Someone has trained themselves to relax.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' rearranges LEARNTTO; 'to' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tolerant person puts up with others' ways without fuss, being relaxed and accepting.

clue.text: Sailing boat seen in seaway in extremis — it's rough

indicators.note: seen in places one piece inside the other
in extremis means at the extremes, so only the outer letters are used

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A yacht caught on a dangerous sea lane in dire straits finds conditions choppy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in extremis' keeps S and Y, the ends of seaway; 'seen in' puts KETCH between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sketchy work is rough and lacking detail, like an outline drawing.

clue.text: A measure of a pickpocket's credit

parts.note: a dip is slang for a pickpocket; the possessive gives the S
tick is British slang for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A thief's loan in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: On tick is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod dipped into a tank or engine to gauge the level of liquid is a measuring tool.

clue.text: Let off for free day

parts.note: spare means free, as in spare time

explanation.surface: Excused from duty for a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To be spared a punishment is to be let off it, pardoned.

clue.text: Report some soldiers delayed

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
late means delayed

explanation.surface: News that certain troops are behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: To relate a story is to tell or report it.

clue.text: About to sit and take it easy

parts.note: re means about, concerning
to pose is to sit for a portrait

explanation.surface: Preparing to settle down and relax.
explanation.definitionFit: To repose is to rest or lie at ease, so it means relaxing.

clue.text: States change — so do these

indicators.note: change signals that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Nations alter, and so do fashions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges STATES; 'these' then refers to things that also change, as preferences do.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal preferences famously shift over time, just as the clue says these things do.

clue.text: Sort of snake in the grass

definitions.text: Sort of snake in the grass

indicators.note: sort of hints at a rearrangement of the next word

explanation.surface: Identifying a type of reptile hiding among the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' rearranges SNAKE. A snake in the grass is a treacherous person, and a grass is an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A treacherous, underhand person or telltale, which a snake in the grass also describes.

clue.text: A good man to torment for the latest news

parts.note: ST, for saint, is a crossword convention for a good man
to oppress is to torment or persecute

explanation.surface: A kindly person is persecuted to make headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase was printed over late items added to a newspaper after the presses had started.
explanation.definitionFit: A late item slipped into a newspaper column at the last moment is the freshest news.

clue.text: Main meal without a starter? It won't please this man

indicators.note: without a starter means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: dinner is the main meal of the day

explanation.surface: Serving dinner without a first course disappoints the hungry diner.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'inner man' is a jocular phrase for one's appetite or stomach, which a meal missing its first course will not satisfy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase inner man is a facetious name for a person's appetite, the part that dinner is meant to please.

clue.text: Elitist minority

parts.note: a select group who regard themselves as specially favoured

explanation.definitionFit: A small privileged group picked out above others, an exclusive elite.
